english: The radio did not accept PTT at {{time}} UTC ({{why}}), so that over was not sent and TX was turned off. Check your PTT method and CAT/port, then turn TX on again.

Nexus did not key the {{mode}} over at {{time}} UTC: Flex native DAX audio is on, but the radio was not yet taking its transmit audio from Nexus over DAX. Nothing was sent and TX was turned off. Nexus finishes setting the radio up within a moment; then turn TX on again.

Nexus did not key the {{mode}} over at {{time}} UTC: Flex native DAX audio is off, but the radio was still taking its transmit audio from DAX, as Nexus had set it, and nothing feeds DAX now. Nothing was sent and TX was turned off. Nexus puts the radio back on its mic input within a moment; then turn TX on again.

Nexus did not key the radio at {{time}} UTC because the transmit audio output would not open ({{why}}). Nothing was sent and TX was turned off. Check Output Device (TX) in Settings (another program may be holding it, or it is unplugged), then turn TX on again.

Nexus did not key the radio at {{time}} UTC: the radio did not take the split frequency ({{why}}), so nothing was sent and TX was turned off. Try Fake It, or None, for Split operation in Settings, then turn TX on again.

Nexus did not key the radio at {{time}} UTC: Nexus could not confirm the radio's SPLIT is off, so nothing was sent and TX was turned off. Turn SPLIT off on the radio, then disconnect and reconnect the radio in Nexus (Settings ▸ Radio ▸ Rig & CAT: set Rig Model to None and Save, then choose your radio again and Save), then turn TX on again.

The radio did not accept PTT off at {{time}} UTC ({{why}}), so TX was turned off. It may still be transmitting: check the radio now. Nexus keeps sending PTT off until the radio accepts it. Turn TX on again once the radio is receiving.

The route carrying an over's audio to the radio (Flex DAX or TCI) stopped at {{time}} UTC in the middle of the over, so the rest of it would have gone out silent. Nexus ended the over there and turned TX off. Turn TX on again to carry on.

notes: Status-bar headline, a warning: one FT8/FT4 over was dropped because the radio keyed too late; TX stays on.

english: This over was dropped: the radio keyed only at {{time}} UTC, {{late}} after your period had ended (slow CAT), so Nexus unkeyed it at once and sent nothing, and left TX on for your next over. Split operation sends the radio its commands before each key, which on a slow CAT link can take seconds: if this keeps happening, check the CAT link and Split operation in Settings.
notes: {{late}} is how long after the end of the station's own period the radio keyed, as Nexus writes it, e.g. "1.2 s": keep it as it is.

english: Nexus did not key the {{mode}} over at {{time}} UTC: the radio was still taking its transmit audio from DAX, as Nexus had set it, not from its mic, so your voice would not have gone out. Nothing was sent. Let go of PTT and Nexus puts the radio back on its mic input within a moment; then press PTT again.
Transmit is off. Press TX On to transmit again.
no microphone is chosen for this radio, so nothing was sent. Choose one in Settings ▸ Radio ▸ Audio.
the chosen microphone is this radio's receive input, so nothing was sent: that would put the band back on the air. Choose your microphone in Settings ▸ Radio ▸ Audio.
the microphone would not open, so nothing was sent. Check that it is plugged in and not held by another program.
the microphone went away during the over, so Nexus unkeyed the radio.
no audio came from the microphone, so Nexus unkeyed the radio.

no sound came from the microphone while you held PTT (only silence, or nothing at all), so the radio was not keyed. Check that the microphone is not muted, and on Windows that Settings ▸ Privacy & security ▸ Microphone lets desktop apps use it.
the over reached its 10-minute limit, so Nexus unkeyed the radio.
the TX watchdog tripped, so Nexus unkeyed the radio and turned TX off.
something else was transmitting (a voice-keyer message, among others), so nothing was sent. Press PTT again when it ends.
the radio stayed on its own mic: Nexus's Flex client asked it to take this computer's audio over DAX, and it had not switched within 2 seconds, so nothing was sent. Press PTT again.

the chosen microphone carries a radio's receive audio (another radio's receive input, or a Flex DAX receive channel), so nothing was sent: that would put the band on the air. Choose your microphone in Settings ▸ Radio ▸ Audio.

the chosen microphone is a loopback or a virtual cable, which carries what this computer plays, Nexus's own transmit audio included, so nothing was sent. Choose your microphone in Settings ▸ Radio ▸ Audio.
transmit stopped being allowed during the over (TX off, outside your licence, a tune, leaving Phone, or another radio, microphone or audio route), so Nexus unkeyed the radio.
the radio was unkeyed or taken over during the over (a radio switch, a CAT hold, or an unkey from elsewhere), so Nexus ended it. Press PTT again.
the radio did not accept the key, so nothing was sent.

the radio's transmit audio output would not open, so the radio was not keyed: it would have gone on the air with no audio. Check that the radio is on with its USB audio connected, and that its TX audio device in Settings ▸ Radio ▸ Audio is the radio's.

the chosen microphone cannot be told apart from an input that may carry the band (a sound server's default input such as default, pulse or pipewire, receive set to the system default, or an input named in a sound configuration file), so nothing was sent: that could put the band on the air. Pick the microphone by its own sound card, and give this radio's receive input its own card, in Settings ▸ Radio ▸ Audio.

Nexus did not play the voice message at {{time}} UTC: the radio did not switch its transmit audio to DAX within 2 seconds, so nothing was keyed. The message was dropped, not held; press its key again.

Nexus did not play the voice message at {{time}} UTC: something else was transmitting or keyed the radio first (your mic or PTT, a tune carrier, another program), so nothing was keyed. The message was dropped, not held.
ATU press dropped at {{time}} UTC: {{why}}; press again.
The radio refused the tune-up at {{time}} UTC (check its tuner is set to the internal tuner).
No answer from the radio to the tune-up at {{time}} UTC; TX stood down in case it is tuning.
No answer from the radio to the tune-up at {{time}} UTC; it may be tuning.
Nexus is repairing this computer’s clock. Nothing starts transmitting until the repair finishes, two minutes at most, so the clock cannot move in the middle of an over.

english: What this means for your contest category

CQ WW rule VIII.2 counts “a CW decoder, DX cluster, DX spotting Web sites … local or remote call sign and frequency decoding technology (e.g., CW Skimmer or Reverse Beacon Network)” as QSO-finding assistance. Using any of them places the entry in Single Operator Assisted (V.A.2) instead of Single Operator (V.A.1).
do_not_translate: <b> | Single Operator | QSO | CQ | CW | DX | VIII.2

english: ARRL contests call it spotting assistance and name “PSKReporter, Telnet, DX spotting websites or bulletin board systems, automated multi-channel decoders”. Single Operator may not use it (HCAT.1.1: “Use of spotting assistance is not permitted.”). Single Operator Unlimited may (HCAT.2.1). ARRL’s glossary defines a multi-channel decoder as software that “displays multiple decoded signals at the same time”. Nexus decodes one signal at a time, so that definition does not describe its CW decoder. It does describe the cluster, RBN and PSK Reporter feeds.
do_not_translate: <b> | Single Operator Unlimited | Single Operator | PSK Reporter | PSKReporter | Telnet | Nexus | ARRL | PSK | RBN | CW | DX | HCAT.1.1 | HCAT.2.1

english: Your radio’s own digital decodes, FT8 and FT4 among them, keep feeding the Needed board in unassisted mode. Neither ruleset sets them apart: both count any technology that identifies a callsign or multiplier as assistance, so do not use the Needed board to find stations if your contest counts them. Your outbound PSK Reporter uploads also keep running, because ARRL says “Generating spotting information for use by other stations is not considered to be spotting assistance.”

A bulk edit never changes the worked call. Nothing is sent from here. A STATION_CALLSIGN replaced with another call is the call a contact is uploaded under, so its upload marks are cleared and the next upload sends it again under the new call, and its LoTW, eQSL and QRZ confirmations, matched under the old call, are cleared; paper QSL cards stay. Filling in a blank STATION_CALLSIGN, clearing one, or adding or removing /P clears no upload mark or confirmation. But a contact with no STATION_CALLSIGN is uploaded under the call in Settings, so a fill or a clear can change the call a contact is sent under to a service it has not been sent to yet: the confirm names those. Every other field keeps its upload marks and confirmations.

If the Parsec session that was connected drops, or its log can no longer be read, Nexus stops a latched PTT, continuous RTTY or PSK, and Tune, exactly as their own Stop does, and says why. Logs the contact from your dial, exactly as the Phone and CW log panels do. On the downlink of a satellite LoTW lists — the one you are working, or the one you last worked until you pick another — Nexus tags it for you: it writes the ADIF PROP_MODE and SAT_NAME fields, so the contact counts toward LoTW satellite credit and Nexus’s own satellite totals. Anything else is logged as an ordinary contact, and on 2 m its grid counts toward your terrestrial VUCC, which a satellite contact does not earn. To tag one yourself, add both fields — one without the other is refused at signing.

Some of that is normal: when the squelch opens partway through a burst the start of the packet is lost, and a part-heard packet can never pass. It is only a fault if nothing ever decodes — in which case check the rig is on {{channel}} in FM.{{advice}} Last burst peaked {{burst}}; live {{level}}.

The burst is CLIPPING (peaked {{peak}}, {{samples}} sample(s) at the rails) — lower the rig's USB AF output level, or the Windows input level for that device. Packet survives a lot of clipping, so this costs headroom rather than decodes, but there is no reason to run into the rails.

Heartbeats are going out on schedule, on a random free slot between 500 and 1000 Hz. Click to stop the schedule.

english: Auto-reply is on, but TX is off — nothing keys; a reply is shown as “would have replied”. Enable TX (the header pill) to let replies go out.

notes: Tooltip on the JS8 cockpit's AUTOREPLY chip while it is on and TX is on: the automatic replies will really go out. SNR?, GRID?, INFO?, QUERY and MSG are JS8 command words and are not translated.

Relay is on, but TX is off — nothing keys. Enable TX (the header pill) to relay.

english: Relay is on, but with AUTOREPLY off a relay is put in the message box for you to send, and nothing keys by itself. Turn AUTOREPLY on to relay on the air.

Heartbeat acknowledgements are on, but TX is off — nothing keys. Enable TX (the header pill).

Heartbeat acknowledgements are on, but they answer only while AUTOREPLY is on, as in JS8Call. Turn AUTOREPLY on.
Heartbeat acknowledgements are on, but they answer only while heartbeat networking (HB NET) and AUTOREPLY are both on, as in JS8Call. HB NET sends nothing by itself.
Two acts, where JS8Call has one: this switch is the second, the header’s TX pill is the first, and the chip reads ARMED only while both are on.
Not armed: nothing from you for {{min}} min, so the idle watchdog holds it. Your next send, switch, speed choice, or Read or Delete in the Inbox brings it back.
Would reply to {{to}} — TX is off, nothing keys: {{text}}

english: The rig must take its SSB audio from USB (its menu for the transmit audio source). Most radios come set to the front microphone, and then an over sends the shack's microphone instead of you.
notes: "USB" here is the computer connection: the rig takes its transmit audio from the USB cable. It is not the USB sideband.

english: The microphone is blocked for this site. Allow it in the browser's settings for this site (the icon at the left of the address bar), then turn the microphone on again.
notes: Shown when this site is blocked from the microphone in the browser. "The icon at the left of the address bar" is the browser's site-information icon (a padlock or two sliders) at the start of the web address.

english: Your computer's privacy settings are blocking the microphone for the browser. On Windows, open Settings ▸ Privacy & security ▸ Microphone and turn on microphone access, including for desktop apps. On a Mac, open System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone, turn the browser on, and reopen it. Then turn the microphone on again.
notes: Shown when the computer itself (Windows or macOS privacy settings) blocks the browser from the microphone. The menu names are Windows' and macOS's own: use the names those systems show in Italian.

english: The browser's question about the microphone was closed without an answer. Turn the microphone on again and choose Allow.
notes: "Allow" is the button in the browser's own question: use the word the browser shows in Italian.

english: No microphone was found on this computer. Plug one in, then turn the microphone on again.
The microphone was found but could not start. Another program may be using it: close that program, then turn the microphone on again.
The browser could not get the microphone ({{name}}). Check the browser's settings for this site and the computer's microphone settings, then turn the microphone on again.
notes: {{name}} is the browser's own name for the error, such as NotAllowedError, and stays in English.

english: This browser cannot send the microphone on this stream.
The browser is still processing the microphone (echo cancellation, noise suppression or automatic gain), which can make your voice sound worse on the air.
PTT is held but your microphone is off, so nothing is transmitted. Turn the microphone on to talk.
The rig shows no power out while your voice is arriving. Set its SSB audio source to USB (its menu for the transmit audio source).
notes: "USB" here is the computer connection: the rig takes its transmit audio from the USB cable. It is not the USB sideband.

english: Your connection stalled, so the transmission stopped.
notes: "Transmission" here is the radio transmission (the rig on the air).

english: Your audio stopped arriving, so the transmission stopped.
notes: "Transmission" here is the radio transmission (the rig on the air).

english: Control was lost, so the transmission stopped.
notes: "Transmission" here is the radio transmission (the rig on the air).

english: The transmission ended at its 10-minute limit. Press PTT again to carry on.
The TX watchdog stopped the transmission.
The station's audio changed, so the transmission stopped. Press PTT again.
Time to give your call sign.
notes: A reminder shown while the operator is transmitting: the rules require giving your call sign at least every ten minutes and at the end of a contact.

english: Remember to give your call sign at the end of the contact.
Still there? The stream ends in a minute unless you click.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air. Shown after fifteen minutes with no click, key press or PTT from this browser.

On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air. The one button on the "Still there?" prompt.

english: Nobody answered “Still there?”, so the stream ended.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air. Use the same words for "Still there?" as in remote.stream.idle.prompt.

english: The stream ended because station control was lost.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: This station can't stream yet. Update Nexus at the shack and turn streaming on there.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: Your Remote access has ended, so the stream can't start.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: Remote access was switched off for this account, so the stream ended.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: Too many tries. Wait a minute, then start the stream again.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: Your Remote access over the internet has ended, so the stream works only on the shack's own network. Connect this device to the same network as the station, then start the stream again.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: Streaming on the shack's own network needs a newer Nexus at the shack. Update Nexus there, then start the stream again.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: The station's reply was not encrypted end to end, so the stream was refused.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: This browser can't show the stream. Use a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: The stream stops while this tab is in the background. Start it again when you're back.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: The connection to the station was lost. Start the stream again.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: Streaming is off at the shack. In Nexus there, turn on “Stream this station from my browser” (Settings → Remote), then start the stream again.
notes: Quotes another control by name: "Stream this station from my browser" is the on-screen text of settings.remoteStream.label. Translate the quote and that control exactly the same way, or the hint names a control the screen does not show.

english: Another browser is streaming this station. You can stream once it ends.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: The station could not use this browser's stream request. Use a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission — pick a word that cannot be read as transmitting on the air.

english: Nexus at the shack is asking you to approve this browser. Approve it there if it shows this browser’s key, below, then start the stream again.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission. Shown when this browser was approved before streams checked its key.

english: This browser’s key has changed, so Nexus at the shack asks you to approve it again. Approve it there if it shows this browser’s key, below, then start the stream again.
notes: On the Remote stream page: Nexus at the shack shown live as a picture in a web browser, and operated from it. "Stream" here means that live picture, never a radio transmission. Shown when the key this browser signs with is not the one Nexus at the shack approved.

english: This reply was not signed with your station's key, so it may not have come from your station. Nothing was connected.
Nexus at the shack did not sign its reply, so this browser can't tell it came from your station. Update Nexus at the shack, then start the stream again.
This station’s key has changed, so nothing was connected. Return to your stations to compare the new key with “This station’s key” in Nexus at the shack.
notes: “This station’s key” is the start of the line where Nexus at the shack shows its key (remote.thisStationKey): use the same words, so the operator can find it there.

english: The station isn't online. Check that Nexus is running at the shack with Remote turned on, and that the computer is awake.
notes: On the Remote stream page, when the station has not answered for several seconds: Nexus at the shack is closed, Remote is off there, or the computer is asleep.

Button on a station card on the Remote page, and on its audio-only page: hear the station's receive audio in the browser, with no picture. The same word as remote.audio.start. The same English text "Listen" is used by 3 different keys (e.g. remote.audio.start, remote.account.role.listen) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: Ready. Press Listen to hear the station's receive audio.
notes: On the Remote page's audio-only view, before the audio starts. "Listen" is the button's own label (remote.listen.open).

english: The station couldn't start just now. Press Listen again.
notes: On the audio-only view, when the station could not start just now. "Listen" is the button's own label (remote.listen.open).

english: Nexus at the shack is asking you to approve this browser. Approve it there if it shows this browser’s key, below, then press Listen again.
This browser’s key has changed, so Nexus at the shack asks you to approve it again. Approve it there if it shows this browser’s key, below, then press Listen again.
This station isn't sending its receive audio. Check that Nexus at the shack is up to date and has the radio's audio input set.
notes: On the audio-only view, when the station does not offer its receive audio (an older build, or no radio audio input set).

english: Ready. Stream to see and operate Nexus at the shack, or Listen for its audio only.
notes: One sentence on a station card on the Remote page, for a browser approved for that station. "Stream" and "Listen" are the card's two buttons (remote.stream.open, remote.listen.open): use the same words. "Stream" means Nexus shown live as a picture in a web browser, never a radio transmission.

english: This browser isn't approved for this station yet. Press Stream, and Nexus at the shack asks you to approve it.
notes: On a station card for a browser not approved for that station yet. Pressing Stream asks Nexus at the shack, which shows a question there. Use the same word as the Stream button (remote.stream.open). "Stream" means Nexus shown live as a picture in a web browser, never a radio transmission.

english: Waiting for approval at the shack: Nexus there asks whether to let “{{browser}}” stream. Approve it if it shows this key: {{key}}.
notes: On a station card while Nexus at the shack asks whether to approve this browser. {{browser}} is the browser's own name, such as "Chrome on Windows"; {{key}} is a code like A1B2 C3D4 E5F6 0718 that the operator compares on both screens. "Stream" means Nexus shown live as a picture in a web browser, never a radio transmission.

english: Waiting for approval at the shack: Nexus there asks whether to let “{{browser}}” stream. Approve it there.
notes: On a station card while Nexus at the shack asks whether to approve this browser. {{browser}} is the browser's own name, such as "Chrome on Windows". "Stream" means Nexus shown live as a picture in a web browser, never a radio transmission.
A short code on the station card for this browser's request; Nexus at the shack shows the same code beside it.

The name a browser gives itself when it asks a station to approve it, shown at the shack: for example "Chrome on Windows". {{browser}} is a browser's product name and {{system}} an operating system's; neither is translated.
The name a browser gives itself when its type cannot be read, shown at the shack in "Let {{browser}} stream this station?".
A small label beside the beta warning (remote.beta.notice) on the Remote site and in Nexus. Keep it one short word.

english: Remote streaming is a beta feature. Access could be revoked at any time.
notes: On every station card on the Remote site, on the stream page, and beside the streaming switch in Nexus. "Streaming" means Nexus shown live as a picture in a web browser, never a radio transmission; "revoked" means the service can stop this account using it.

english: Station data unavailable. Refresh or reconnect.
Click a signal to tune it
Waiting for the account to claim this station
Confirm this station in your browser first — the Remote page is asking whether to attach it. Then approve here again.
The Remote service holds a different key for this station than the one it signs its stream with, so browsers refuse its stream. Use Revoke station access, then pair this station again.
Unlock your operating system’s credential store and try again. Remote stays disabled if its credential cannot be stored securely.
This station's access was revoked from a browser, so it has stopped connecting. Nothing here is broken — pair it again below when you want it back.
Your Remote trial has ended, so this station could not be added to the account. Your radio, your log and your settings are untouched.
Remote access for this account has been switched off, so this station could not be added to it. This is not the trial running out. Your radio, your log and your settings are untouched.
A Remote trial is one per callsign, so set your station callsign in Settings → Station first, then pair this station again. Your radio, your log and your settings are untouched.

The callsign in Settings → Station is not an active US licence in the FCC's licence list, so this station could not be added. Check it for a typo. A new licence takes about a day to appear there. Your radio, your log and your settings are untouched.

This callsign has already had a Remote trial under another account, so this station could not be added. If this is your callsign, write to support from the email address on your licence. Your radio, your log and your settings are untouched.
This computer has already had a Remote trial under another account, so this station could not be added. Your radio, your log and your settings are untouched.
Adding a station to Remote needs a newer Nexus. Update Nexus, then pair this station again. Your radio, your log and your settings are untouched.

This email address already has a Remote trial running under a different sign-in, such as Google instead of a password, so this station could not be added. In your browser, sign out, sign in the way you did the first time, then pair this station again. Your radio, your log and your settings are untouched.
Enter a name for this station to sign in or pair.

notes: Short label on: the station list of the remote browser. The same English text "Rename" is used by 3 different keys (e.g. logbook.filters.rename, settings.cw.macros.profiles.rename) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

Short label on: the station list of the remote browser. The same English text "Cancel" is used by 32 different keys (e.g. logEntry.sent.moved.cancel, logbook.import.preview.cancel, logbook.parkStates.cancel) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: This code expires after ten minutes.

Remote stays on when Nexus restarts: if it was on when Nexus closed, it turns itself back on and reconnects. Approved browsers keep what you allowed. Turn off Remote only disconnects: turning it back on restores what each approved browser had.
Remote can only come back after this computer restarts if Nexus starts too. Start Nexus when you sign in to this computer?
Start Nexus when I sign in
This computer did not let Nexus start at sign-in. You can try again in Settings.
Approved until {{until}} UTC. Using the station from this browser keeps it approved, up to {{limit}} UTC.
This approval ends {{until}} UTC. Approve the browser again to keep it.

notes: In Nexus at the shack, beside a browser's name. {{key}} is that browser's device key as a short fingerprint, like 3F2A 9C1B 77E0 4D12; the browser shows the same one, and the operator compares the two before approving it. The same English text "Key {{key}}" is used by 2 different keys (e.g. lanWindow.stationKey) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: This browser can’t stream until you approve it again here. First check this key matches the one the browser shows.
notes: In Nexus at the shack, under a browser that is approved but whose key has not been checked here. "Stream" means Nexus shown live as a picture in a web browser, never a radio transmission.
Beside a browser in that list that is waiting for approval. "Stream" means Nexus shown live as a picture in a web browser, never a radio transmission.

Button beside an approved browser in that list: removes its approval. The same English text "Remove" is used by 11 different keys (e.g. logbook.tools.bulk.remove, settings.streetMaps.remove, settings.radios.remove.action) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: Asks to operate this station over the internet.
This computer can’t connect until you approve it again here. First check this key matches the one Nexus shows on it.
Sign in with your Nexus Remote account in the browser that opens. There is no code: each of your other devices is then added when you sign in on it.
Waiting for you to sign in, in the browser that opened…
Signing in to Nexus Remote is not available in this build yet. Pair with a code instead.
The sign-in did not finish. Try again.
notes: The same English text "The sign-in did not finish. Try again." is used by 2 different keys (e.g. lanWindow.internet.reason.signInFailed) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: Another sign-in is already open on this computer. Finish or close it, then try again.
Your account already has two stations. Remove one on the Remote page first.
Sign in again to keep adding devices: the key your station's sign-in was checked with has been retired.

Nexus could not read its list of computers removed here, so it adds no device by its sign-in and takes no computer on this network. Press Reset network identity under Network identity below. A reset removes every paired computer, so each one has to be paired again.
Sign in with the account this station belongs to.
Added by signing in as you: {{name}} ({{what}}), key {{key}}.
Added for someone you invited ({{role}}): {{name}} ({{what}}), key {{key}}.

notes: The same English text "Got it" is used by 4 different keys (e.g. fieldDay.workIn.hint.dismiss, phone.keyer.flexDax.dismiss, firstContact.close) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: Waiting for you to allow it to transmit.
That device is no longer waiting to transmit. It was removed, or it was not added by signing in.
The Remote service says this device is yours, but Nexus could not confirm it. Approve it only if you added it yourself.
Removed here. The Remote service hears of it when this station is back online.
Removed. Nexus could not confirm whether this computer also shows as another row under Devices. Check the list, and remove it there too if it does.
Every computer, phone and browser that can reach this station, under whoever it belongs to.
Added by signing in, not yet known whose
Listening and tuning only. Transmit waits for you to press Allow to transmit, or about {{minutes}} min.

notes: The same English text "Details" is used by 3 different keys (e.g. dxped.calendar.view.list, pathWhy.detail.summary) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: Invite someone by the address they sign in with. Their devices are added when they sign in. Someone invited to operate transmits with your station, under your callsign: you stay responsible as its licensee.

notes: The same English text "Operate" is used by 4 different keys (e.g. features.category.operate, features.operate.label, amp.operate) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.
The same English text "Listen" is used by 3 different keys (e.g. remote.audio.start, remote.listen.open) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: Someone invited to operate can do all you can from another computer: transmit under your callsign, edit, export or delete your log, upload with your saved logins (LoTW signed with your certificate), spot under your call and read your Winlink mail. Invite to operate only someone you would hand the shack to.
notes: Shown under the Role choice while inviting someone, when Operate is picked.

The same English text "Remove" is used by 11 different keys (e.g. logbook.tools.bulk.remove, settings.streetMaps.remove, settings.radios.remove.action) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: Also taken off this network, since Nexus could not tell whose they were: {{names}}. Whoever uses them signs in on them again to come back.
This station has invited as many people as it can. Remove someone first.

notes: A fold in Settings ▸ Remote access that holds the pairing and permission options. The same English text "Advanced" is used by 3 different keys (e.g. setup.finish.license.advanced, settings.rigControl.advanced.title) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.
Button: approve a browser for this station, in the list and in the question Nexus shows when a browser asks to stream.

Title of the question Nexus shows at the shack when a browser asks to stream. {{browser}} is the browser's own name, such as "Chrome on Windows". "Stream" means Nexus shown live as a picture in a web browser, never a radio transmission.

english: A browser signed in to your Remote account asks to stream this station and operate it as you would here, transmit included. Approve it only if this key matches the one the browser shows: {{key}}.
notes: Under that title. {{key}} is a code like A1B2 C3D4 E5F6 0718 that the operator compares with the one the browser shows. "Remote" is the product's name (Nexus Remote). "transmit included" is the radio sense: through the stream the browser can key the rig.

english: This browser was approved before, but it can’t stream until you approve it again here. When it streams, it can operate this station as you would here, transmit included. Approve it only if this key matches the one the browser shows: {{key}}.
notes: Under that title, for a browser approved before its key was checked here. {{key}} is a code like A1B2 C3D4 E5F6 0718 that the operator compares with the one the browser shows. "Stream" means Nexus shown live as a picture in a web browser, never a radio transmission; "transmit included" is the radio sense: through the stream the browser can key the rig.

english: Nexus on {{platform}}, signed in to your Remote account, asks to operate this station over the internet as you would here, transmit included. Approve it only if this key matches the one Nexus shows on that computer: {{key}}.

Nexus on {{platform}} was approved before, but it can’t connect until you approve it again here. Connected, it can operate this station as you would here, transmit included. Approve it only if this key matches the one Nexus shows on that computer: {{key}}.

notes: Button in that question: refuse the browser.

english: A browser signed in to your Remote account. It can listen and tune now, and transmit waits for you. Allow it only if this key matches the one the browser shows: {{key}}.
Nexus on {{platform}} signed in to your Remote account. It can listen and tune now, and transmit waits for you. Allow it only if this key matches the one Nexus shows on that computer: {{key}}.

notes: The same English text "Not now" is used by 6 different keys (e.g. reveal.notNow, update.notNow.label, lanWindow.operateNo) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: Lets Nexus on another computer on this network operate this station, with no internet needed. Pair each computer here once; it keeps access until you remove it.

notes: One-word control on: Settings ▸ Station ▸ Remote access ▸ Remote over this network. Out of context this could be a noun or a verb — open that screen (or read the key name) before choosing the Italian word.

Short label on: Settings ▸ Station ▸ Remote access ▸ Remote over this network. The same English text "Starting…" is used by 5 different keys (e.g. settings.connectWeb.url.pending, map.street.sheet.running.starting, lanWindow.opening) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

english: Listening at {{address}}. Only computers paired here can connect.

Off: this station has no network key it can read. Press Reset network identity under Network identity below, then turn this on again. A reset removes every paired computer, so each one has to be paired again.
notes: Names another control: "Reset network identity" is the on-screen text of remote.lan.reset. Translate the name and that control exactly the same way, or the hint names a control the screen does not show. Names another control: "Network identity" is the on-screen text of remote.lan.resetTitle. Translate the name and that control exactly the same way, or the hint names a control the screen does not show.

english: Off: remote control was ended here. Turn this on again when you want it.
Not listening: {{address}} is not this computer’s address right now. Nexus listens there again when it is back, or choose another network.
Not listening: choose which of this computer’s networks to listen on.
Not listening: another program is using its port.
Not listening: this computer is not on a private network.
Not listening: it could not start on this computer.
Type this code in Nexus on the other computer. It works once, within ten minutes.
Whoever types it in time can operate this station, transmit included, so keep it to yourself.
Only at the station itself: this can’t be done through a stream.
Eight computers are paired already. Remove one to pair another.

Nexus could not read or keep this station’s network key and paired computers in your operating system’s credential store. Press Reset network identity under Network identity below. A reset removes every paired computer, so each one has to be paired again.
notes: Names another control: "Reset network identity" is the on-screen text of remote.lan.reset. Translate the name and that control exactly the same way, or the hint names a control the screen does not show. Names another control: "Network identity" is the on-screen text of remote.lan.resetTitle. Translate the name and that control exactly the same way, or the hint names a control the screen does not show.

english: Nexus could not do that. Try again.
Resetting makes a new network key and removes every paired computer. Use it if this computer’s key may have been copied, then pair your computers again.
This station and the other computer both need Windows, for now.
The first time this is turned on, Windows asks whether Nexus may use networks. Allow Private networks only.
notes: "Private networks" is the choice Windows offers when it asks whether a program may use the network: use the words Windows shows in Italian.

Short label on: Settings ▸ Station ▸ Remote access ▸ Remote over this network. The same English text "Network" is used by 3 different keys (e.g. gettingStarted.radio.shot.netLabel, setup.rig.conn.network.label) — each can take a different Italian word, so choose the one that fits THIS screen.

One-word control on: Settings ▸ Station ▸ Remote access ▸ Remote over this network. Out of context this could be a noun or a verb — open that screen (or read the key name) before choosing the Italian word.

english: Virtual adapters and VPNs are not offered: other computers on this network can’t reach this one through them.
Windows won’t let other computers find this station by name here, so type its address on the other computer.
A guest network, or one that keeps its devices apart, stops other computers reaching this one, and Nexus can’t tell that from here.
When Windows asks whether Nexus may use this network, allow Private networks only.
notes: "Private networks" is the choice Windows offers when it asks whether a program may use the network: use the words Windows shows in Italian.

english: Windows calls this network Public, so its firewall keeps other computers out. If this is your own network, make it Private in Windows Settings ▸ Network & internet.
notes: "Public" and "Private" are Windows' names for the two kinds of network, and Settings ▸ Network & internet is Windows' own menu: use the names Windows shows in Italian.

english: Windows Firewall blocks Nexus on this network, as it does after its question is cancelled. Allow Nexus on Private networks in Windows Security ▸ Firewall & network protection ▸ Allow an app through firewall.
notes: "Private networks" and Windows Security ▸ Firewall & network protection ▸ Allow an app through firewall are Windows' own names: use the names Windows shows in Italian.

english: Windows Firewall blocks every incoming connection on this network, so no other computer can reach this station.
This computer’s firewall is set by an administrator’s policy, which may keep other computers out. Ask whoever manages it to allow Nexus.
Windows Firewall blocks new programs on this network without asking. Allow Nexus on Private networks in Windows Security ▸ Firewall & network protection ▸ Allow an app through firewall.
notes: "Private networks" and Windows Security ▸ Firewall & network protection ▸ Allow an app through firewall are Windows' own names: use the names Windows shows in Italian.

english: That address isn’t on this computer’s network. Join the station’s network, or check the address the station shows.
The station’s computer answered, but nothing listens at that port: Remote over this network is off there, or on another port. Check the address the station shows.
notes: Names another control: "Remote over this network" is the on-screen text of remote.lan.switch. Translate the name and that control exactly the same way, or the hint names a control the screen does not show.

Leave this off unless you know you need it. Nexus normally puts the radio in its DATA submode (DATA-U / USB-D / PKTUSB) for FT8, FT4, RTTY-AFSK and SSTV, because on most rigs that is the only mode where the USB codec reaches the transmitter. Turn this on and Nexus commands plain USB/LSB for those modes instead, and stays there — through band changes and when you call a station. Correct if your transmit audio goes in the microphone path, as with an interface wired to the mic jack (some RIGblaster models) — or if you simply prefer plain USB to the DATA submode (for its wider receive passband, say) and your rig is set to send its USB-codec audio in SSB, which on many modern rigs (FT-991A, IC-7300 and the like) is a single menu item. Either way the rig has to put the audio you're feeding onto the air in plain SSB: where it does not — the codec feeds only the data port and nothing carries in SSB — plain SSB takes audio from the mic and the radio transmits no RF at all, a red TX light and nothing on the air. Per radio, since it depends on how that rig is cabled and set. True FSK RTTY is unaffected — it keeps the rig's own RTTY mode.

Keeps this radio in the data submode for the whole time the SSTV receiver is running, instead of only while a picture is queued or going out — FM-D / DATA-FM on an FM channel, and USB-D / LSB-D on HF. Off by default, which is what Nexus does today: it commands the data submode around a send and puts the radio back in plain FM or SSB in between, so a rig parked on an SSTV calling channel keeps dropping out of the data mode. That revert is deliberate — an SSTV send once keyed a data mode into an FM repeater input — but it is the wrong answer if you sit on an SSTV calling channel for the evening. Stop the receiver before you go back to voice. The receiver keeps running after you leave the SSTV screen, and while it runs this radio is held in the data submode, where transmit audio comes from the data port and your microphone modulates nothing. Per radio, since it depends on how that rig is cabled and what you use it for.

Step the amplifier to the band you are on, without being asked. Off by default — this is the one amplifier control that acts on its own. It never moves the amplifier while you are transmitting, and it steps one band at a time, checking where the amplifier actually is after each one rather than assuming it got there. ⚠️ If your amplifier already follows the radio through its own band-data cable, as most SPE installations do, leave this off: the hardware is doing the same job, and two things steering one band is worse than either alone.

After Nexus keys the radio it waits this long before sending any audio, so an amplifier keyed from the radio has time to switch before RF reaches it. 0 = off. It helps only where Nexus’s audio makes the RF: SSB and data modes, the computer or remote microphone on Phone, soundcard CW, and Tune when Nexus makes the tune carrier. It cannot help with FM, AM, FSK RTTY, CW sent by the radio itself, the radio’s own microphone, VOX, Tune on a Flex or TCI radio that makes its own tune carrier, or an amplifier keyed by RF sense: use the radio’s own TX delay for those. A program transmitting through Nexus’s TCI server gets no delay from Nexus; use that program’s own Tx delay. FT8 already has half a second of quiet at the start of each over, so this changes nothing there unless the radio is slow to key. FT4 keeps WSJT-X’s own timing and ignores this. FT2 overs start later by this much. On FT1 a long delay trims the end of each over at the slot boundary, and it still decodes. On Phone, letting go of PTT keeps the radio keyed until the speech you had already spoken has been sent.

english: 30 s — sparse pings, more to stack

MSK144 sends a 72 ms message over and over, so a single meteor trail lasting a tenth of a second can carry the whole thing. Shorter periods turn the exchange around faster during a shower; longer ones give the decoder more frames to stack when pings are sparse. Both stations must use the same period.

MSK144 transmits for nearly the whole period, sending the same 72 ms frame hundreds of times — that is how meteor scatter works, and a contact can take many minutes of apparent silence. The audio frequency is fixed at a 1500 Hz centre; the signal is 1 kHz wide, so there is nowhere to tune it. Shorthand (MSK40) messages are off, matching WSJT-X’s default.

Required, and it has to be real. WSPR reports are published to a public propagation database that other operators draw conclusions from, so a wrong figure corrupts their data as well as yours. The beacon stays silent until this is set. 23 = 200 mW, 30 = 1 W, 37 = 5 W, 43 = 20 W.

0 = use the transmit-% schedule. Otherwise your slot in a coordinated rotation: stations agreeing on the same slot count and each taking a different slot never transmit at the same time, because the assignment is fixed by UTC. A rotation needs at least 2 slots.
A one-station rotation is no rotation — Round Robin needs at least 2 slots, so it is off and the transmit-% schedule applies.
